correctness.rationale: For regular nilpotent B the full centralizer is Fq[B], so a nonzero commuting nilpotent A has a unique polynomial f(B) of valuation k and necessarily almost-rectangular Jordan type [n]_k. Conversely J_n^k realizes every such type. The standard endomorphism-algebra radical quotient gives number q^(dimCent(A)-k) of nilpotent commuting matrices, using the Fine-Herstein q^(m*m-m) count in each matrix factor. Double counting conjugators for f(J_n) similar to A gives each f a fiber of |C_GL(A)|/((q-1)q^(n-1)), independent of f. Division by the nilpotent centralizer count gives Phi_r Phi_(k-r) for nonzero almost rectangular A; zero A has its own correct boundary formula. Actual package file check.py was executed and its output byte-compared with check_output.txt: 18 partition instances, 5192 nilpotent centralizer elements, 3293 regular occurrences, 31 uniform polynomial fibers.

originality.rationale: The verified contribution is the simultaneous fixed-matrix probability for all Jordan partitions and uniformity of the unique polynomial fibers for regular nilpotent commuting partners. Published papers read in relevant sections classify possible commuting Jordan types or simultaneous-similarity forms, not this complete finite-field parameter-fiber law. The known orbit/stabilizer, Fine-Herstein, and unit centralizer counts are acknowledged, and their combination makes the novelty relatively narrow; possible implicit prior implication remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed published counting theorem for pairs of commuting nilpotents could imply the exact regular-fiber formula by specialization.
The fiber count is a concise orbit-stabilizer calculation from known centralizer sizes; an earlier paper may have already drawn this consequence.
The classic Fine-Herstein count is taken as a proved external theorem, not reproved in the package.

value.rationale: For the natural sampling space of nilpotent commuting partners of a fixed nilpotent matrix, the result determines when the unique largest nilpotent Jordan orbit occurs and exactly how frequently for every finite field and every Jordan partition. It also determines a uniform law for the unique polynomial relation and an exact invariance under common scaling of almost-rectangular block lengths. Such shape-sensitive densities and uniform parameter fibers are not provided by a possible-Jordan-type list or unit-centralizer count; they support finer probabilistic and enumeration questions about commuting nilpotent pairs. This is a natural complete binary-event classification, not an arbitrary tiny case, though a stronger existing count would remove its originality.
